order.why_here: FIFO built from two LIFO stacks: reverse each item exactly once, lazily, and learn amortised cost over an item's whole life.
The mirror image: a queue cannot reverse, only rotate, so each push turns the line until the newcomer is at the front.
Time only moves forward, so expired pings leave from the front in arrival order and the queue is exactly the window.
A queue in k fixed slots: move a head index instead of the data, wrap with % k, and keep a count to tell empty from full.
The same ring with both ends movable: the front grows backwards by stepping head counter-clockwise before writing.
Two queues of turn times: the earlier front bans the other and rejoins as index + n, so rounds fit in one ordered line.

see_also.why_here: A fixed-size window queue with a running sum: append the new value, pop the oldest, adjust the sum.
Number of Recent Calls with many hits per timestamp: a time-window queue of (time, count) buckets plus a running total.
The monotonic deque: the front expires as the window slides, the back is popped when a newcomer dominates.
A monotonic deque over prefix sums: starts leave the front once used, and dominated starts leave the back.
A heap picks the next task while a FIFO cooldown queue holds used tasks stamped with the time they may run again.
Multi-source BFS: every rotten orange starts in the queue, and each queue layer is one minute of spreading.
Multi-source BFS from all zeros at once: the queue's layers are the distances to the nearest zero.
BFS over an implicit graph of words: the queue holds the current frontier, and the first time the target is reached is the shortest.
0-1 BFS: free moves go on the deque's front, cost-1 moves on its back, so the front is always the cheapest cell.
